strings.name: Xavi
strings.role: Footballer and Netherlands men’s head coach
strings.summary: Xavi’s passing, positioning and control of tempo made him central to Barcelona and Spain’s possession football. He won eight Spanish league titles and four Champions Leagues at Barcelona, plus a World Cup and two European Championships with Spain. After coaching Al-Sadd and Barcelona, including the 2022–23 league title, he became Netherlands head coach in August 2026 on a contract through the 2030 World Cup.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A core figure in Spain’s World Cup and European Championship victories who spread possession football internationally.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: A model midfield organiser
strings.highlights.h1.text: Reading space, offering short passes and controlling tempo helped Barcelona win four Champions Leagues.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Joined Barcelona’s youth system in 1991 and developed through La Masia into the senior team.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Spain’s golden period
strings.highlights.h2.text: Won Euro 2008, the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012; was named player of Euro 2008.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Netherlands head coach
strings.timeline.t1.text: The KNVB appointed him to succeed Koeman through the 2030 World Cup, his first senior national-team head coaching job.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Barcelona coaching tenure ended
strings.timeline.t2.text: The club decided to change coaches, ending his first-team tenure begun in 2021.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Spanish title as coach
strings.timeline.t3.text: Led Barcelona to the 2022–23 league championship, applying his playing experience in management.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Returned to Barcelona
strings.timeline.t4.text: Left Al-Sadd to coach Barcelona and undertake the team’s rebuilding.
strings.timeline.t5.title: From player to coach
strings.timeline.t5.text: Ended his playing career in Qatar and became Al-Sadd head coach.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Left Barcelona for Qatar
strings.timeline.t6.text: Finished his Barcelona playing years with another treble and moved to Al-Sadd after 767 senior appearances for the Catalan club.
strings.timeline.t7.title: World Cup champion
strings.timeline.t7.text: Was a central midfield organiser as Spain won its first World Cup.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Official first-team debut
strings.timeline.t8.text: Scored against Mallorca in the Spanish Super Cup, beginning seventeen seasons in Barcelona’s senior side.
